AMBER directs secondary particle beams from the Super Proton Synchrotron onto various targets to study hadrons such as protons, antiprotons, pions and kaons.

physics_goals.quote: The first is to determine the rates at which antiprotons are produced in proton–hydrogen and proton–helium collisions.
physics_goals.value: Determine antiproton production rates in proton-hydrogen and proton-helium collisions, measure the proton radius with muons, and measure quark and gluon momenta in pions and kaons

summary.plain: AMBER is the successor to COMPASS at CERN. It directs beams of muons, protons, pions, kaons and antiprotons at targets to measure antiproton production (relevant to dark-matter searches), the proton's charge radius and the quark and gluon momenta inside pions and kaons. It started taking data in 2023.
summary.technical: Apparatus for Meson and Baryon Experimental Research (NA66) on the SPS M2 beam line in EHN2, built on the upgraded COMPASS two-stage spectrometer: phase 1 antiproton production in p+H2 and p+He, proton-radius measurement with high-energy muons and pion/kaon Drell-Yan structure; phase 2 intense kaon beams (strange-meson spectroscopy, Primakoff reactions). Approved 2020, data taking from 2023, SPS stopped for LS3 on 2026-08-31.
